context.concept_name: Operate an EC2 instance after external cloud compute-lifecycle preparation

coverage.learning_objective: Operate an EC2 instance in AWS and inspect its supplied instance profile: an instance role is an IAM role whose temporary credentials provide the instance's AWS permissions; an instance profile is the container used to attach that role to EC2. Inspecting the supplied profile is not independently configuring role trust.

required_facts.statement: Launching an EC2 instance requires choices such as AMI, instance type and network placement; an AMI supplies the initial software image.
In the launch workflow, use the approved AMI, subnet and supplied IAM instance profile, then inspect the created instance’s ID and settings.
An instance profile contains an IAM role and attaches it to EC2; applications on the instance can use that role’s temporary credentials.
Inspect instance state and status checks to distinguish lifecycle state from reported host or instance health.

teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: The launch request for an EC2 lab instance is ready, but an operator must connect the approved choices with the resource that was actually created. Treat launch inputs, instance identity, lifecycle state and health evidence as distinct parts of the check.

teaching_blocks.title: The operating model
teaching_blocks.content: Launching an EC2 instance requires choices such as AMI, instance type and network placement; an AMI supplies the initial software image.

teaching_blocks.title: How the check works
teaching_blocks.content:
In the launch workflow, use the approved AMI, subnet and supplied IAM instance profile, then inspect the created instance’s ID and settings.

An instance profile contains an IAM role and attaches it to EC2; applications on the instance can use that role’s temporary credentials.

Inspect instance state and status checks to distinguish lifecycle state from reported host or instance health.

teaching_blocks.title: Work through one sandbox case
teaching_blocks.content: Use the exercise's approved AMI, instance type, subnet and supplied IAM instance profile in the launch workflow. The AMI supplies the initial software image; the instance profile attaches its role so applications can use temporary role credentials. After launch, record the created instance ID and compare its settings with the supplied choices. Next inspect instance state and status checks. If the state is running but a status check reports a problem, retain both observations: lifecycle state and reported host or instance health answer different questions. Do not replace the health evidence with the fact that a launch request completed. This is operation of the approved instance, not guest-OS configuration or independent role-policy design.

teaching_blocks.title: Do not confuse the evidence
teaching_blocks.content: An instance being in a running lifecycle state does not make status-check evidence redundant. Read state and status checks separately. Similarly, the instance profile attaches the role; it is not a separate set of embedded application access keys.

video_need.reason: Connecting launch inputs with instance identity, lifecycle state and status checks benefits from before-and-after console inspection.

practice_anchor.objective: Launch one EC2 instance using the supplied approved AMI, instance type, network setup and IAM instance profile. Inspect the created instance's ID and settings, identify the IAM role attached through the supplied profile, and inspect lifecycle state and status checks without changing the supplied configuration.
practice_anchor.success: One instance is created with the approved launch choices. Its recorded ID, AMI, instance type, subnet and supplied instance profile match the created resource. The attached IAM role is correctly identified, and lifecycle state and status-check results are recorded separately rather than treating a running state as proof of health.

visual_anchor.purpose: Make the approved launch selections and the resulting instance details visible, including instance ID, AMI, instance type, subnet, supplied instance profile and attached role, with lifecycle state and status-check results shown as separate evidence.

teaching_notes: Require external compute preparation; defer detailed health diagnosis and Linux service configuration.

context.concept_name: Operate S3 object storage for deployment artifacts after external cloud object-storage preparation

coverage.learning_objective: Operate S3 storage for deployment artifacts

required_facts.statement: An S3 object consists of data and metadata and is identified within a bucket by its object key.
Use aws s3 cp LOCAL_FILE s3://BUCKET/KEY --profile NAME --region REGION to upload, and reverse the source and destination to download.
A bucket is created in an AWS Region; verify the intended bucket location and caller access when storing or retrieving an object.

teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: A supplied deployment file must be stored and retrieved from the intended S3 location. Name both the bucket and the object key before transferring it, and keep the operator profile and Region explicit in the operation.

teaching_blocks.title: The operating model
teaching_blocks.content: An S3 object consists of data and metadata and is identified within a bucket by its object key.

teaching_blocks.title: How the check works
teaching_blocks.content:
Use aws s3 cp LOCAL_FILE s3://BUCKET/KEY --profile NAME --region REGION to upload, and reverse the source and destination to download.

A bucket is created in an AWS Region; verify the intended bucket location and caller access when storing or retrieving an object.

teaching_blocks.title: Work through one sandbox case
teaching_blocks.content:
For an illustrative transfer, let LOCAL_FILE be orders-release.zip and let KEY be releases/orders-release.zip in the approved bucket. Substitute the supplied bucket, profile and Region into the upload command. To download the same object, reverse the source and destination: the S3 reference becomes the source and the local file path becomes the destination. The object key identifies the object within its bucket; do not compare only the local filename when confirming which object was retrieved. Check the intended bucket location and caller access as part of the exercise. The command template teaches the two transfer directions without introducing an independent bucket-policy or object-recovery workflow.

Trace the upload and download endpoints before executing: upload has the local file as source and s3://BUCKET/KEY as destination; download reverses them. If the exercise expects releases/orders-release.zip, retrieving a different key is not a successful verification even when a file arrives locally. The intended location and transfer direction are checks you can make from the command arguments before inspecting its outcome.

teaching_blocks.title: Do not confuse the evidence
teaching_blocks.content: The object key is scoped within a bucket. A familiar key string alone does not identify the intended storage location. Check the bucket's Region and the caller's access rather than assuming either from the file's name.

video_need.reason: A short transfer demonstration helps connect local paths with bucket/key paths, but the two direction templates are sufficient in text.

practice_anchor.objective: Upload orders-release.zip to releases/orders-release.zip in the supplied sandbox bucket, then retrieve that same object using an explicit operator profile and Region.
practice_anchor.success: The upload and download succeed for the intended bucket/key. Both commands specify the supplied profile and verified bucket Region, and the retrieved artifact matches the supplied file.

live_code.required_skill: Construct and execute S3 copy commands in both directions, identifying the bucket/key and checking supplied bucket-location and caller-access evidence.
allowed_syntax: aws s3 cp LOCAL_FILE s3://BUCKET/KEY --profile NAME --region REGION
aws s3 cp s3://BUCKET/KEY LOCAL_FILE --profile NAME --region REGION
live_code.starter_state_intent: Provide orders-release.zip, an approved sandbox bucket, a configured operator profile, the bucket's Region, and evidence that the caller can upload and retrieve releases/orders-release.zip. Supply a separate local destination for retrieval and an artifact-comparison result without requiring additional command syntax.
live_code.observable_success: Both transfer commands use the same supplied bucket and releases/orders-release.zip key, explicitly include the supplied profile and verified Region, and complete successfully. The supplied comparison confirms that the downloaded file matches orders-release.zip.

visual_anchor.purpose: Make the two transfer directions visible with annotated commands: local source to S3 bucket/key for upload, then the same S3 bucket/key to a local destination for download. Highlight the explicit profile and Region in both commands.

teaching_notes: Require external object-storage preparation; leave versioning and retention to later concepts.

context.concept_name: Publish workload metrics with interpretable dimensions

required_facts.statement: A custom CloudWatch metric is identified by its namespace, name and dimension combination.
Publish a metric with put-metric-data, specifying namespace, metric name, value and the intended dimensions.
Each distinct dimension combination identifies a distinct metric; query the same combination that was published to select the intended series.

teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: An orders workload reports a metric, but the operator must select the same series that was published. The metric name is only part of that identity. Namespace and the full dimension combination also matter.

teaching_blocks.title: The operating model
teaching_blocks.content: A custom CloudWatch metric is identified by its namespace, name and dimension combination.

teaching_blocks.title: How the check works
teaching_blocks.content:
Publish a metric with put-metric-data, specifying namespace, metric name, value and the intended dimensions.

Each distinct dimension combination identifies a distinct metric; query the same combination that was published to select the intended series.

teaching_blocks.title: Work through one sandbox case
teaching_blocks.content:
Suppose the supplied metric is QueueDepth in namespace Lab/Orders with dimensions Environment=sandbox and Service=orders. Publish the supplied value with put-metric-data using that namespace, name and dimension combination. When querying, select that same combination. A second publication with Environment=staging and Service=orders identifies a distinct metric, even though its name is also QueueDepth. In the exercise record, write the namespace, name and dimensions beside the observed value. That makes the comparison about a particular series rather than a name shared by several series. These dimension values are illustrative workload labels; do not add new dimension combinations just to make the example more elaborate.

Consider a query using Environment=sandbox but omitting the supplied Service=orders dimension. It is not the same dimension combination as the example publication, so it does not identify that series by the stated identity rule. Compare complete combinations in the evidence record. This prevents a result from the staging series or another published combination from being described as the sandbox orders value.

teaching_blocks.title: Do not confuse the evidence
teaching_blocks.content: Querying by a familiar metric name is not enough to establish that you selected the intended series. Each distinct dimension combination identifies a distinct metric. Compare the published and queried combinations, not just the displayed metric name.

video_need.reason: Publishing and locating distinct dimension combinations makes metric-series identity clearer than a metric-name-only screenshot.

practice_anchor.objective: Emit the supplied QueueDepth value in namespace Lab/Orders using put-metric-data with exactly the supplied dimensions Environment=sandbox and Service=orders.
practice_anchor.success: The publication specifies Lab/Orders, QueueDepth, the supplied value and both intended dimensions without adding dimension combinations. The exercise record associates the observed value with that complete metric identity.

visual_anchor.purpose: Show published and queried metric identities side by side: namespace Lab/Orders, name QueueDepth and the complete dimension combination. Make the matching sandbox orders series distinguishable from the staging orders series and a query that omits Service=orders.

teaching_notes: Do not introduce dimension-cost claims or alarm thresholds not present in the brief.
